summary.headline: Godrej Agrovet Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue rose 9% YoY to INR2,333 crore; PBT before exceptionals up 16.8% to INR87 crore, with FY27 guided to early double-digit revenue and mid-teens PBT growth.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 consolidated revenue of INR2,333 crore (+9% YoY) and PBT before non-recurring items of INR87 crore (+16.8%), driven by volume growth and margin management. For FY26, revenue crossed INR10,000 crore at INR10,233 crore (+9%) and PBT before exceptionals rose 17.2% to INR569 crore, with working capital reduction lifting ROCE from 16% to 20%. Animal Nutrition volumes grew 15% YoY in Q4 (cattle feed +24%), Astec reached EBITDA breakeven for FY26, and Crop Care stayed weak on co-marketing channel inventory. Management guided to early double-digit consolidated revenue growth and mid-teens PBT growth for FY27, while flagging the Middle East conflict and a below-normal monsoon forecast as variables.

segments.name: Animal Nutrition
segments.commentary: Q4 volumes +15% YoY, cattle feed +24%, with margins expanding across the portfolio on new products, East and Central India share gains, and raw material cost reconfiguration. Pet food manufacturing income of about INR9.5 crore sits in other income, flattering segment margin.

segments.name: Oil palm
segments.commentary: FY26 saw record area expansion, strong volume growth and an all-time high oil extraction ratio. Q4 is seasonally weak (about 60,000 tonnes of FFB out of 6.37 lakh tonnes annually) but margins held up on OER and realizations.

segments.name: Crop Care
segments.commentary: Q4 impacted by carry-forward of co-marketing channel inventory, lowering in-house product volumes; partly offset by specialty products. FY27 guided as a recovery year with very high double-digit growth in revenue and profit from Q2 onwards.

segments.name: Astec LifeSciences
segments.commentary: Achieved EBITDA breakeven in FY26; Q4 revenue and EBITDA grew strongly on CDMO volumes, realizations and utilization. Enterprise molecules about 48% of FY26 revenue, CDMO (new products) about 52%; exports about 53% of revenue.

segments.name: Creamline Dairy
segments.commentary: Revenue up about 5% YoY excluding bulk sales in Q4; profitability pressured by elevated milk procurement costs. Value-added product salience rose to about 40% from 38%.

segments.name: Godrej Foods
segments.commentary: EBITDA margins improved significantly in Q4 on Live Bird and Yummiez; branded revenue salience above 80% in FY26. Live Bird trading being phased out.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth targeted at early double-digit, volume-led; PBT growth targeted at mid-teens.
Animal Nutrition: double-digit volume-led revenue growth targeted in FY27.
Crop Care: recovery year, with very high double-digit growth in top line and bottom line; full recovery from Q2 as Q1 laps prior-year co-marketing inventory.

Oil palm: early double-digit volume growth targeted; area expansion to beat FY26 record; specialty fat refinery rolling out May 2026, meaningful from H2 FY27; value-added share targeted at 50-55% of portfolio by FY31.
Astec: about 15% top-line growth targeted, CDMO growing faster; CDMO salience to be held at 52-53%, with a possible stretch to about 20% growth. Margins described as intact.
Capex FY27 about INR350-400 crore (75-80% growth); expected post-capex cash surplus of INR100-125 crore in FY27; ROCE ambition not quantified.
Dividend payout about 48%, to be decided annually with promoters; no commitment given.
capex_capacity: FY27 capex close to INR400 crore; medium-term capex around INR350 crore a year, with 75-80% growth capex; about 50% of capex goes to oil palm.
Oil palm: about 50% of trees are juvenile (0-4 years, unproductive); planting ramp-up expected to drive a productivity 'demographic dividend' over the next five years.
Specialty fat refinery in oil palm to be rolled out in May 2026.
Astec: 47% of imports for the year were sourced from China; backward integration done for most enterprise molecules and being pursued with CDMO partners.
Godrej Foods: entering momos and frozen chicken in FY27; Live Bird trading exiting over 4-5 years, with live birds kept as a sourcing backbone.
demand_pricing: Animal feed: share gains claimed in East and Central India; Type 1 higher-yield products and Dhanlaxmi brand scaling in Maharashtra and Karnataka; Bypro Plus upgrade in South. Elevated milk prices are shifting farmers from unbranded to branded feed.
Milk procurement prices expected to ease gradually from Q2 FY27, normalizing thereafter; this is a key pressure point for Creamline.

Palm oil: management is managing quarter-to-quarter after Middle East conflict changed palm oil price models; palm oil is correlated with crude oil. Management said a prolonged Middle East war is negative for crop protection but positive for oil palm.

Crop Care: two new launches in FY27 - Ashitaka (maize herbicide, launched Dec 2025) and TAKAI (rice multi-crop insecticide). Together they are expected to contribute 16-18% of revenue in FY27, versus about 3% in FY26.
Astec: pricing has stabilized as Chinese competition and local demand firm; Q4 showed volume and realization gains; early CDMO leads emerging.
Monsoon: IMD and Skymet forecast below-normal monsoon, with August-September the likely stress period; management is not yet changing guidance and expects oil palm to be largely unaffected this year.

qa_highlights.question: What FY27 revenue and profit growth can be expected?
qa_highlights.answer: Early double-digit consolidated revenue growth and mid-teens PBT growth, volume-led; Iran war remains an overhang.

qa_highlights.question: How will a weak monsoon affect segments?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance kept for now; management says El Nino impact is hard to call by geography. Oil palm not expected to be hit this year, and South region normal would limit Crop Care impact. Animal feed correlates mainly with milk yield.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Astec board and management change, and the structure of the chemicals business?
qa_highlights.answer: Vishal Sharma joined as Non-Executive Chairperson and Mathew Eipe as Independent Director; Arijit Mukherjee is now Executive Director. Structure review is ongoing, with an update expected over the next two to three quarters; minority interests to be protected.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the pet food income in Animal Nutrition, and is it revenue or profit?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR9.5 crore is profit from contract manufacturing of pet food for GCPL's front-end business. Revenue is not recognized by GAVL under accounting norms; the income is booked in other income.

qa_highlights.question: What are the FY27 capex, working capital and cash flow expectations?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex about INR400 crore for FY27, leaving a cash surplus of about INR100-125 crore; medium-term capex about INR350 crore, mostly growth capex, with about 50% going to oil palm.

qa_highlights.question: What is Astec's outlook for growth and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: About 15% top-line growth targeted, with CDMO growing faster and margins intact; CDMO salience held at 52-53%, with a possible about 20% growth stretch.

qa_highlights.question: How much oil palm earnings come from value-added products, and how is downside protected?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 65-70% of last year's profit jump came from internal efforts, with pricing under 30%. Value-added share targeted at 50-55% by FY31, with the specialty fat refinery from H2 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the shift in Q4 extraction and dividend policy discussed?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 OER was 20.77% vs 19.76% a year earlier on a small base. Dividend payout was about 48%; the dividend will be decided with promoters each year based on results.

risks_watch: Below-normal monsoon, with August-September stress forecast from IMD and Skymet; impact on animal feed via milk yields and on Crop Care by geography.
Middle East conflict and crude oil link to palm oil prices; a palm price correction could hit oil palm earnings.
Milk procurement costs remain elevated until Q2 FY27 and may pressure Creamline Dairy.
Astec's reliance on China for about 47% of imports and rupee depreciation, though net exporter status offers a partial natural hedge.
Astec chemicals structure review pending over the next two to three quarters, plus strategic reviews of shrimp, seeds and cattle genetics businesses.
Crop Care recovery depends on Q1 FY27 clearing prior-year co-marketing inventory and on the new launches (Ashitaka, TAKAI) scaling.

summary.management_tone: Confident on the FY26 numbers, Animal Nutrition, Astec's CDMO momentum and the oil palm extraction ratio. Noticeably cautious on the Iran war, palm oil pricing ("playing it quarter-to-quarter") and the El Nino/monsoon outlook, where guidance was kept unchanged. Evasive on Astec's chemicals structure, which management said is "too premature" to comment on, and on the dividend, which will be decided with promoters each year.
